note:
A fresh check found these problems in this version. Fix each one, and keep everything that is right:

A student can pick it from that word alone without counting particles. Consider plain 'A gold bar' or 'A gold ring', or add 'pure' to a distractor, such as 'Pure, clear salt water'.

rejected.title: Pure substances and mixtures
card: Pure substance
It is made of only one kind of particle. Pure water has only water particles, and pure gold has only gold particles.
Mixture
It has two or more kinds of particle that are not joined together. Sand and water, or salt and pepper, are mixtures.
Solution
A solution is a mixture in which a solute is dissolved evenly in a solvent. In salt water, the salt is the solute and the water is the solvent.
A mixture can be a solid, a liquid or a gas. Air is a mixture of several gases, and clear salt water is still a mixture, because it holds two kinds of particle.
rejected.remember: Pure: one kind of particle. Mixture: two or more kinds, not joined together.

a.q: Which sample contains only one kind of particle?
opts: A pure gold bar
A glass of salt water
Soil from a garden bed
Air in a bicycle tyre
a.why: Pure gold has only gold particles, so it is a pure substance. Salt water looks the same all through, but it has salt and water particles, so it is a mixture. Air is a mixture of several gases.
a.clue: Count how many kinds of particle each one has.

b.q: Jo stirs sugar into hot tea until the tea looks clear and the same all through. Which statement is correct?
opts: It is a solution, with sugar as the solute
It is a pure substance, because it looks the same
It is a solution, with sugar as the solvent
It is a pure substance, because the sugar vanished
b.why: The sugar dissolves evenly in the liquid, so the tea is a solution. The sugar is the solute, and the liquid it dissolves in is the solvent. Looking the same all through does not make it pure, because it still has sugar and water particles.
b.clue: Which particles are still in the cup after the sugar disappears?
